record.paper_title: Lubrication Approximations for Surface Tension Driven Interfaces: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Can one prove finite-time droplet pinch-off in the lubrication approximation for a liquid jet falling from a nozzle, where h is the outer surface radius, x is the axial coordinate, v is the leading-order axial velocity, and the reduced model approximates the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes free-surface equations with gravity, surface tension, density, and viscosity? The target is an analytical proof that the reduced system develops a finite-time singularity corresponding to droplet breakup, rather than only numerical evidence for such a singularity.

evidence.quote: However, no proof of this fact exists.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the lubrication (slender-jet) approximation for a viscous liquid jet falling from a nozzle under gravity, surface tension, and inertia. Let h(x,t) > 0 denote the outer free-surface radius of the axisymmetric jet and let v(x,t) denote the leading-order axial velocity, where x is the axial coordinate and t is time. After non-dimensionalization with density ρ, dynamic viscosity μ, surface tension coefficient σ, and gravitational acceleration g, the reduced one-dimensional system obtained by asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional axisymmetric Navier–Stokes free-surface equations takes the form

  ∂_t(h^2) + ∂_x(h^2 v) = 0,
  ρ (∂_t v + v ∂_x v) = -σ ∂_x κ(h) + (3μ / h^2) ∂_x(h^2 ∂_x v) + ρ g,

where κ(h) is the leading-order mean-curvature term in the slender-jet approximation (for example κ(h) = 1/h − ∂_xx h / (1+(∂_x h)^2)^{3/2}, or a standard reduction thereof), posed on a suitable axial interval with boundary conditions modeling a nozzle at one end and a free end below.

Prove analytically that, for an appropriate class of smooth initial data with h > 0, there exists a finite time T* < ∞ at which the solution develops a pinch-off singularity, i.e.

  liminf_{t → T*-} inf_x h(x,t) = 0,

corresponding to droplet breakup. The goal is a rigorous mathematical proof (not merely numerical or asymptotic evidence) that this reduced lubrication system produces a finite-time zero of h.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature provides extensive numerical and asymptotic (self-similar) evidence for finite-time pinch-off in the slender-jet lubrication model, and rigorous results exist for related but distinct models (e.g., a Hele-Shaw thin-neck model where pinch-off in finite or infinite time has been proved, and fourth-order thin-film equations where weak solutions are constructed past possible singularities). However, no rigorous analytical proof of finite-time pinch-off for the slender-jet lubrication system describing a liquid jet from a nozzle appears in the literature; surveys continue to list this as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On Singularity Formation in a Hele-Shaw Model
status_evidence.snippet: For any P > 2 and any smooth positive initial datum, the solution pinches off in either finite or infinite time.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous pinch-off results exist for a related Hele-Shaw thin-neck lubrication model, but not for the full slender-jet system.

status_evidence.title: The Lubrication Approximation for Thin Viscous Films: Regularity and Long-Time Behavior
status_evidence.snippet: For strictly positive initial data, even if a finite-time singularity h → 0 does occur, there exists a weak nonnegative solution for all time.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous results for fourth-order thin-film equations address weak-solution continuation past singularities but do not prove finite-time pinch-off for the jet model.

status_evidence.title: Universal Pinching of 3D Axisymmetric Free-Surface Flow
status_evidence.snippet: Self-similar pinch-off solutions are constructed and matched numerically.
status_evidence.claim: Self-similar/numerical evidence for finite-time pinch-off is well established, but a full analytical proof for the slender-jet lubrication system is not provided.
